text: UNION-based SQL Injection is a technique where an attacker uses the SQL <highlight>UNION</highlight> operator to combine results from the original query with a malicious query. This allows attackers to retrieve data from other tables in the database.
Discovering Column Count Using ORDER BY

code:
?id=1 ORDER BY 1--
?id=1 ORDER BY 2--
?id=1 ORDER BY 3--

text: Attackers increase the column number until the database throws an error. The highest valid number indicates how many columns the original query returns. The <highlight>--</highlight> (or <highlight>#</highlight>) is used to comment out the rest of the original query.

SQLite UNION injection leverages the <highlight>UNION</highlight> operator to bypass original query results and display data from the <highlight>sqlite_master</highlight> table. This is essential for SQLite environments where traditional <highlight>information_schema</highlight> does not exist.
Extracting SQLite Version and DB Info

code:
UNION SELECT 1,sqlite_version(),3--
UNION SELECT 1,file,3 FROM pragma_database_list--

text: The <highlight>sqlite_version()</highlight> function returns the library version. <highlight>pragma_database_list</highlight> reveals the absolute path of the database file on the server, which can help map the internal directory structure.

code: UNION SELECT 1,name,3 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'--

text: In SQLite, the <highlight>sqlite_master</highlight> table contains the database schema. Filtering by <highlight>type='table'</highlight> allows us to find the names of all user-created tables.

code: UNION SELECT 1,sql,3 FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='users'--

text: Unlike MySQL, SQLite stores the original <highlight>CREATE TABLE</highlight> statement in the <highlight>sql</highlight> column. Reading this reveals the column names needed to dump data.
If the application only displays one result field, use <highlight>||</highlight> (pipe operator) for concatenation or <highlight>GROUP_CONCAT()</highlight> to pull all rows into a single string.

code:
UNION SELECT 1,username || ':' || password,3 FROM users--
UNION SELECT 1,GROUP_CONCAT(username),3 FROM users--

text: Important Rules for UNION SQL Injection

title: Requirements for UNION Injection
items: The number of columns in the UNION query must match the original query
Data types in the columns must be compatible with the original columns
The original query should be made to return 'nothing' (e.g., id=-1) so only the injected data shows
At least one column from the original query must be visible on the webpage

text: UNION-based SQL Injection is a powerful method for data extraction. In <highlight>SQLite</highlight>, the reliance on <highlight>sqlite_master</highlight> and the <highlight>||</highlight> operator are the key differences from MySQL. Mastering these shifts allows for successful enumeration across different database engines.
